title: Court view layout
question: Kiln stays the look, and scoring is live, rally by rally. Pick how a scorekeeper's court screen is arranged, steer one, or re-roll.

options.label: Match card and queue
options.lineage: the scorer's clipboard: this match on top, the running order underneath
options.thesis: One large match card with each team's score and big +1 / −1 buttons, then the court's queue of what's next.
options.viewport: A slim ink band with 'Court 3' and a switcher to other courts; the match panel fills the screen: team names, huge Unbounded scores side by side, +1 under each in thumb reach, −1 smaller, Finish match in ember; Up next rows below the fold.
options.risk: The most conventional of the three; the queue competes a little with the score for attention.

raised.raise: When the court is handed a new match, it slides up from the queue into the panel and stays lit until the scorekeeper's first tap, so a change is never missed.

options.label: Court from above
options.lineage: the court itself, seen from the umpire's stand
options.thesis: The phone becomes the court: a net line across the middle, each half belongs to one team, and tapping a half scores for that team.
options.viewport: Top half: team A's name and giant score, the whole half a +1 target; a net line with the court number across the middle; bottom half: team B the same; a small −1 chip in each half's corner; Finish match and Up next below the fold.
options.risk: A stray tap anywhere on a half scores a point, so −1 and the saved-state indicator must be obvious.

options.label: Flip scoreboard
options.lineage: the flip-number scoreboard on a stand at courtside
options.thesis: Two columns like a courtside flip board: team name on top, giant numerals that flip on each point, big +1 below each.
options.viewport: Court number and match on a thin ink strip; two tall columns fill the screen, each a team name over a split flip-card numeral; under each, a +1 as wide as the column and a smaller −1; Finish match spans the bottom.
options.risk: The flip motion is decoration if it slows reading; it must be quick and off under reduced motion.
